What are Pragmatic Trials?

Pragmatic trials are designed to test interventions in real-world conditions, focusing on:

- **Real-world effectiveness** rather than controlled efficacy
- **Broad patient populations** with minimal exclusion criteria
- **Routine clinical settings** rather than specialized research environments
- **Practical outcomes** that matter to patients and clinicians
- **Rapid implementation** of findings into clinical practice

## Key Differences at a Glance

| Metric               | Pragmatic Trials (e.g., RECOVERY)    | Traditional Explanatory Trials                                                                      |
| -------------------- | ------------------------------------ | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Cost per Trial       | Lower due to existing infrastructure | [$48-225 million](https://www.anjusoftware.com/insights/eclinical/clinical-trial-costs/)            |
| Time to Results      | Weeks to months                      | [5-7 years average](https://www.fda.gov/patients/drug-development-process/step-3-clinical-research) |
| Participants         | Large (e.g., 47,000+ in RECOVERY)    | [Typically 500-3000](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC6248200/)                         |
| Implementation Speed | Hours to days                        | Months to years                                                                                     |
| Patient Population   | Diverse, real-world                  | Highly selected                                                                                     |
| Setting              | Routine clinical practice            | Specialized research centers                                                                        |
| Generalizability     | High                                 | Limited                                                                                             |

![Side-by-side comparison illustrating the structural differences in cost, speed, and scale between pragmatic and traditional explanatory trials.](/assets/images/pragmatic-vs-explanatory-trials/pragmatic-vs-explanatory-trials-section-key-differences-comparison-bw-academic.jpg)

## Cost Analysis

### Traditional Explanatory Trials

![A bar chart comparing average costs across clinical trial phases and a comparison of per-patient costs between specific therapeutic areas and the general average.](/assets/images/pragmatic-vs-explanatory-trials/pragmatic-vs-explanatory-trials-section-traditional-explanatory-trials-bw-academic.jpg)

- Average phase costs ([source](https://www.sofpromed.com/how-much-does-a-clinical-trial-cost)):
  - Phase 1: $4 million
  - Phase 2: $13 million
  - Phase 3: $20 million

- Per-patient costs vary by therapeutic area:
  - Blood disorders: $200,000-422,000
  - Average across areas: {{< var traditional_phase3_cost_per_patient >}} {{< var traditional_phase3_cost_per_patient_cite >}}

## Speed and Efficiency

### RECOVERY Trial Metrics

![An infographic illustrating the RECOVERY trial's rapid timeline from concept to policy implementation alongside its massive scale across 200+ hospitals and 47,000+ participants.](/assets/images/pragmatic-vs-explanatory-trials/pragmatic-vs-explanatory-trials-section-recovery-trial-metrics-bw-academic.jpg)

- 9 days: Concept to first patient enrollment [@recovery-trial-dexamethasone-results]
- 10 weeks: First life-saving treatment identified [@landray-recovery-trial-quote]
- 3 hours: Results to policy implementation [@landray-recovery-trial-quote]
- 47,000+ participants across 6 countries [@recovery-trial-summary-quote]
- 200+ hospital sites [@recovery-trial-summary-quote]
- 10 major results obtained [@recovery-trial-summary-quote]
- 4 effective COVID-19 treatments identified [@recovery-trial-summary-quote]

### Traditional Trial Metrics

![Key pain points in traditional clinical trials, highlighting the 7.2-year average development timeline and the high rates of enrollment and site-level failure.](/assets/images/pragmatic-vs-explanatory-trials/pragmatic-vs-explanatory-trials-section-traditional-trial-metrics-bw-academic.jpg)

- Average time from phase 1 to approval: [7.2 years](https://www.bio.org/sites/default/files/legacy/bioorg/docs/Clinical%20Development%20Success%20Rates%202006-2015%20-%20BIO,%20Biomedtracker,%20Amplion%202016.pdf)
- 80% of trials fail to meet enrollment timelines [@clinical-trial-enrollment-timelines]
- Up to 50.0% of research sites enroll one or no patients [@clinical-trial-enrollment-timelines]

## Clinical Impact

### RECOVERY Trial

![A visual summary of the RECOVERY trial results for dexamethasone, illustrating the 35 percent mortality reduction for ventilated patients and the timeline from results to saving one million lives globally.](/assets/images/pragmatic-vs-explanatory-trials/pragmatic-vs-explanatory-trials-section-recovery-trial-bw-academic.jpg)

- Dexamethasone findings [@recovery-trial-dexamethasone-results]:
  - 35% reduction in mortality for ventilated patients
  - Estimated 1 million lives saved globally [@recovery-trial-summary-quote]

- Implementation within hours of results
- Real-world effectiveness immediately apparent

### Traditional Trials

- [14% success rate from phase 1 to approval](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC6092479/)
- Average 7 years from discovery to clinical practice
- Limited real-world applicability due to strict inclusion criteria

## Advantages of Pragmatic Trials

![An infographic highlighting the four key pillars of pragmatic trial advantages: Generalizability, Resource Efficiency, Implementation Speed, and Statistical Power.](/assets/images/pragmatic-vs-explanatory-trials/pragmatic-vs-explanatory-trials-section-advantages-of-pragmatic-trials-bw-academic.jpg)

1. **Better Generalizability**

   - Results apply to broader patient populations
   - Findings directly relevant to routine clinical practice
   - Higher external validity

2. **Resource Efficiency**

   - Uses existing healthcare infrastructure
   - Lower per-patient costs
   - Faster recruitment and completion

3. **Implementation Speed**

   - Rapid translation to clinical practice
   - Immediate real-world validation
   - Reduced lag between evidence and practice

4. **Statistical Power**

   - Larger sample sizes possible
   - More diverse patient populations
   - Better representation of real-world outcomes
